Definition: from the base of G2476; a head of grain (as standing out from the stalk):--ear (of corn).
BiblicalUsage: The ear of corn is the head of grain standing out from the stalk. The disciples plucked the ears of corn on the Sabbath and ate, rubbing them in their hands, and the earth brings forth fruit of herself, first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the ear of corn shows the kingdom growing in order: blade, then ear, then full corn, and the disciples' hunger was met on the way.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
